solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Orchestral movement not working, give in

parts.note: a machine that is down is out of action
to bow is to submit or yield

explanation.surface: A musician refuses to play part of a symphony, then caves in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests a section of a symphony, but here it is a stroke of a string player's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke drawing the bow downward across the strings is a physical motion made by orchestral string players.

clue.text: Avoid nothing

definitions.meaning: to dodge something by ... down out of its way
a batsman's score of zero in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman out without scoring makes a duck, from the egg-shaped zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to dodge, and in cricket it is a score of zero.

clue.text: One complaining when footballer's grabbed hard

indicators.note: grabbed means the footballer holds the other letter inside

parts.note: a winger is a footballer who plays on the flank
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A footballer moans after being roughly tackled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who whines or grumbles persistently, a moaner.

clue.text: Desirable to roll up sail, out to drop anchor?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rolling up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a jib is a triangular foresail

indicators.note: to drop means a piece is removed from the word

parts.note: taken as the word itself before cutting
the anchor of a relay team runs last, so this is the final letter

explanation.surface: Sailing advice: furl the canvas and head out to moor.
explanation.walkthrough: JIB read upwards gives BIJ; OUT loses its last letter, the 'anchor', leaving OU.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate-agent word for a small but elegant and attractive home, so appealing.

clue.text: Insect finding crumb on each set of books

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, a crumb
NT is the New Testament, a collection of biblical books

explanation.surface: Someone finds a bug in breadcrumbs spread over a library.
explanation.definitionFit: A common name for the termite, a pale wood-eating social insect.

clue.text: Farewell speech originally without conclusion?

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word speech

parts.note: a conclusion is an end
off can mean lacking, as when a dish is off the menu

explanation.surface: A leaving speech that never quite reaches its ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean the speech lacks an ending, but it is a synonym, as food you've gone off is something you do without.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a farewell gathering or ceremony marking someone's departure.

clue.text: Some training relative needs to pen sheep

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the sheep sits inside the relative

parts.note: sis is short for sister
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A farm relative must corral a sheep as part of an exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominal exercises done lying down and raising the torso, a form of physical workout.

clue.text: Architect left residing in loathsome country home?

parts.note: John Nash designed Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion

indicators.note: residing in means one piece lives within the other

parts.note: vile means loathsome

explanation.surface: An architect leaves a hideous rural house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country home' suggests a manor, but means the home of country music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tennessee city is the capital of country-and-western music, so it is that genre's base.

clue.text: Stretch too far above ladder

parts.note: over means above
a ladder in tights is a run

explanation.surface: Climbing above a ladder overreaches.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is British for a run in tights or stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed a set limit or time, spreading beyond what was intended.

clue.text: Expect trouble — from a catfight?

parts.note: a phrase predicting a fierce row is read literally as cats scrapping and tearing out tufts of hair

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for an imminent heated quarrel is pictured as an actual fight between cats.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom warning that a furious argument is about to break out.

clue.text: Overpriced establishment, bit common

parts.note: a clip is a short extract, a bit of a film
joint, as in joint ownership, means shared or common

explanation.surface: A rip-off venue described as somewhat vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for a nightclub or bar that fleeces customers with exorbitant prices.

clue.text: Fine total

definitions.meaning: fine as in delicate and see-through, like gauzy fabric
total as in utter or complete, as in absolute nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both translucent, delicate fabric and something absolute or complete.

clue.text: I speed up and give impromptu, impressing conductor finally, Italian maestro

indicators.note: impressing means pressing into, so one letter is set inside the jumble
impromptu means improvised, so the letters are freely rearranged
finally points to the closing letter of the word conductor

explanation.surface: Someone urges a conductor to play faster and improvise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impromptu' shuffles I SPEED UP and GIVE; 'impressing' puts R (end of 'conductor') among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineteenth-century composer of Aida and La Traviata, a great Italian master of opera.

clue.text: One moving quickly to secrete objects, petty larcenist primarily?

definitions.text: One moving quickly to secrete objects, petty larcenist primarily?

indicators.note: to secrete is to hide away, so the initials are tucked inside

parts.note: a shifter is someone who shifts, moves quickly

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letters of objects, petty and larcenist

explanation.surface: A deft thief hiding stolen goods, essentially a small-time crook.
explanation.walkthrough: O, P, L hidden in SHIFTER build the answer, and the whole clue describes a store thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steals goods from a store, a classic petty thief.

clue.text: In sport, time is going fast

indicators.note: In tells us one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: hurling is an Irish field game played with sticks

explanation.surface: During a game, time is running out quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: HURLING is a fast Irish stick-and-ball game; T goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurtle is to rush along at great speed, so the participle means moving rapidly.

clue.text: Overwhelming success gets recounted ultimately in fiction

parts.note: to land something is to get or secure it

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the falsehood

parts.note: a lie is a fiction

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of recounted

explanation.surface: A triumph that is retold until it becomes a tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recounted' hints at an election recount, but just gives its last letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: An election won by a huge majority, hence a crushing victory.

clue.text: Doctor on call: exactly the same?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: Two physicians on duty who look identical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the medic on call, but it is the signal to rearrange ON CALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Clones are genetically identical copies, so the adjective describes things identical to their source.

clue.text: Coming across fish, old mog fed

indicators.note: fed means put into, so the cat goes inside the fish

parts.note: ling is a cod-like sea fish
mog is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: An old cat is given some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Mog, or moggy, is everyday British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding or discovering something, which is what coming across it means.

clue.text: Country, note, surrounded by water

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the note within the body of water

parts.note: a pond is a small body of water
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A nation described as a musical note encircled by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central European nation whose capital is Warsaw.

clue.text: Case of demoiselle being into drink, is this?

definitions.text: Case of demoiselle being into drink, is this?

indicators.note: being into means placed inside the drink

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

indicators.note: case of means the outside letters of demoiselle

explanation.surface: A young lady who enjoys drinking, is this what she is?
explanation.walkthrough: DE, the outside of 'demoiselle', goes into LATTE; the whole clue then describes a hard-drinking young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a boisterous young woman who drinks heavily and behaves loutishly.

clue.text: Fix trouble — check parts fit

indicators.note: parts means separates, so the check splits the other two pieces

parts.note: to do something up is to fix or arrange it
to ail is to trouble or afflict
to vet is to check thoroughly

explanation.surface: Repair advice: sort out the problem and make sure the components match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' reads as a noun, components, but it is a verb: VET separates DO from AIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To join neatly, like interlocking carpentry wedge joints, hence to fit together harmoniously.

clue.text: Star soldier, God of war

parts.note: a soldier ant is a caste of warrior ant
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A celebrated warrior described as a war deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The bright red supergiant in Scorpius, one of the night sky's brightest points.

clue.text: Trader more vulgar, might you say?

indicators.note: might you say signals a word that matches another in speech

parts.note: grosser means coarser or more vulgar

explanation.surface: A merchant asked if he is coarser.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper dealing in food and household goods, a kind of retailer.

clue.text: Inexperienced competitor on river, is one's concern great?

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the preceding piece

parts.note: the Indus is a great river of Pakistan
a trialist is a player being tried out for a team, not yet established

explanation.surface: A novice athlete beside a river wonders whether his worry matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' reads as worry, but here it means a business: this person runs a big one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who owns or manages a large manufacturing business, a company being a concern.

clue.text: Problem children

definitions.meaning: a matter of dispute or concern, as in a burning question
offspring, as in dying without heirs

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a point of contention and also a person's offspring.

clue.text: Small and sweet, one's eyed

definitions.note: one that has eyes, a definition by description

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
pud is short for pudding, a British dessert

explanation.surface: A tiny, cute person gets stared at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyed' reads as looked at, but means having eyes, the buds on a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial for a potato, a tuber whose buds are called eyes.

clue.text: Old king and tiresome infants initially play together

parts.note: Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the ancient Egyptian king

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of tiresome and infants

explanation.surface: An ancient pharaoh and some wearisome children start a game together.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning all performers, so everyone plays at once.

clue.text: Snatch and rip off fastener

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thief grabs something and tears away a clasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap passing under the jaw that holds a helmet or hat securely in place.

clue.text: Plant life no better, all ending the wrong way for animal

indicators.note: the wrong way means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside grass

indicators.note: all ending points to the final letter of each of the words life, no and better

explanation.surface: A gloomy verdict that plant life gets no better and all is going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: REED plus EOR (the last letters of life, no, better) gives REEDEOR; 'the wrong way' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A small European deer species, an example of a wild mammal.

clue.text: Through the ear, visitor took a shot

indicators.note: through the ear means we go by how a word sounds when spoken

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A visitor caught a sound and then fired.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a shot at something is idiomatically to attempt an answer without knowing it.
